items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.author: lairv
items.summary: On November 9, 2026, Anthropic released two versions of its model, Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. Fable 5.2 is generally available today and is available on all paid plans on the Claude Platform, in Claude Code, and on major cloud platforms. Mythos 5.2 is the same model with lighter guardrails, restricted to vetted organizations through Anthropic's Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs for work in biomedical research and defensive cybersecurity. Fable 5.2 is up to 30% faster than its predecessor and cheaper to run, costing $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Mythos 5.2 is limited to organizations that are part of Anthropic's verification programs.

items.title: Payments Canada announces launch of Canada's Real-Time Rail (RTR) payment system
items.author: ocd
items.summary: Payments Canada has announced the launch of Canada's Real-Time Rail (RTR) payment system, set to debut in Q4 of 2026. The RTR will provide a national real-time payment system, enabling instant A2A payments through real-time exchange and clearing and settlement of funds. It will offer real-time, irrevocable payments that clear and settle between financial institutions in real-time, 24/7/365. The RTR will include a centralized fraud service to address challenges faced by other jurisdictions launching real-time payment systems. The launch date has been impacted by current delivery delays, but Payments Canada, its regulators, and member financial institutions remain committed to delivering a safe, secure, and efficient real-time payment system for Canada.

items.title: Foldable Flight: The Best Paper Airplanes
items.author: vismit2000
items.summary: According to Fold 'N Fly, the best paper airplane for distance is The Bird, which can glide for a long distance and has been tested to stay up for over 6 seconds, more than triple the average flight time of less than 2 seconds. Foldable Flight recommends Alpha Lock for its ability to fly extremely far. Instructables provides a step-by-step guide to folding a basic paper airplane, emphasizing the importance of precise folds for optimal performance.

items.title: CoreWeave bond yield tops 16% as AI credit stress rises
items.author: lxm
items.summary: CoreWeave's bond yield has climbed above 16%, as reported by CNBC, amid rising AI credit stress. The yield on its 9.625% bond due in 2032 surpassed 16%, and its credit default swaps spiked above 1,289 basis points on Thursday, higher than their October peak, according to Deutsche Bank. This increase in borrowing costs reflects investor concerns about default risks among AI-linked borrowers.

items.title: Semi-transparent, colored cadmium telluride photovoltaic panels in agrivoltaics
items.author: speckx
items.summary: The sources indicate that semi-transparent, colored cadmium telluride photovoltaic panels have been evaluated in agrivoltaic systems, specifically in trials involving broccoli and strawberry cultivation. The panels transmit wavelengths favorable for plant growth, achieving photosynthetically active radiation transmittance values of 13.2% and 19.2%. While reduced light delays broccoli maturity by 25 days, it maintains comparable fresh biomass to open-field plants. For strawberries, agrivoltaics using CdTe panels with 40% and 70% transparency showed potential for increased fruit revenue and energy self-sufficiency. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on all aspects of the technology's performance and broader implications.

items.title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators
items.author: gf74918
items.summary: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators, reversing a 2023 commitment that such content would not be seen by human reviewers. Updated documentation and blog post edits confirm that connected apps are routed into human review pipelines. Testing demonstrates that this ingestion occurs autonomously during casual conversation without explicit tags and can capture sensitive personal information.

items.title: Muse Ember: Our smallest, most efficient model
items.author: dvaplima
items.summary: Muse Ember is Meta's smallest and most efficient model, scoring 36 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and costing about $0.13 per Intelligence Index task at max reasoning effort. It is competitive across multimodal, agentic, and coding tasks, outperforming similar-class models on AutomationBench-AA and Terminal-Bench 4.0. It is available in all Muse Code subscription plans, optimized for low price-per-task at $0.10 input / $0.50 output per million tokens for up to 200k input tokens, and $0.30 input / $1.50 output for prompts above 200k input tokens. It is recommended for repeated, bounded work and can be paired with Muse Wonder or Muse Spark for more complex workflows.

items.title: TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max
items.author: _benx_
items.summary: Google launched TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, expanding its Tensor Processing Unit series. TPU 8tx is designed for secure and confidential inference, paired with AMD's EPYC CPU, and has 2x lower latency than TPU 8t. TPU 8i Max is built for massive context windows and high compute density per rack workloads, with double the SRAM and HBM bandwidth of TPU 8i. The new TPUs are part of Google's efforts to meet a wide range of use cases for AI as agents scale.

items.title: Time for AVIF everywhere?
items.author: speckx
items.summary: According to Joost de Valk, "you should use both AVIF and WebP on your website. They’re smaller, they’re better. All browsers support them." However, as of December 2024, AVIF cannot be used on social platforms yet, but WebP share images can be safely used everywhere since June 2024. The sources don't provide a definitive answer on when AVIF will be universally adopted for social platforms.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 scores 65 on Artificial Analysis, highest so far
items.author: theanonymousone
items.summary: According to the sources, Claude Fable 5.2 scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, which is the highest score so far. This model, created by Anthropic, places well above average compared to other models, with a median score of 31. It also generated 275 million output tokens, which is higher than the median of 77.7 million. The model leads in five of the nine evaluations in the Intelligence Index, scoring ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Astra.

items.title: A renowned scientist, a deadly snakebite, and a diary that documented it (2025)
items.author: areoform
items.summary: In 2025, Karl P. Schmidt, a renowned Field Museum scientist, was bitten by a snake he was trying to identify. Despite the severity of the bite, he did not seek medical treatment and instead documented his symptoms in a diary. Schmidt wrote that the snake resembled a boomslang and detailed his symptoms hour by hour, including strong nausea and vomiting. He died within 24 hours of the bite. His diary, which he kept while dying, was later referred to as a "death diary" by newspapers.

items.title: Show HN: STE80 Humanizer – de-AI text by writing 80% of the way to ASD-STE100
items.author: Dodaios
items.summary: The STE80 Humanizer is an agent skill that rewrites AI-generated text to remove common 'AI tells' and restructure sentences toward ASD-STE100, a Simplified Technical English standard used in aircraft maintenance manuals. It combines Wikipedia's 26-pattern 'Signs of AI writing' catalog with Andrej Karpathy's idea of writing '80% of the way to ASD-STE100' for clearer, more human-sounding prose. Install it via `npx skills add Dodaios/ste80-humanizer` for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or other agents. ASD-STE100 is a controlled language from 1980s aerospace maintenance manuals, built for mechanics whose first language isn't English, with rules like 20 words per instruction, one idea per sentence, active voice, and about 900 approved words. Karpathy suggested asking an LLM to explain things '80% of the way to ASD-STE100' because the full spec is too stringent for natural prose but makes output more readable.

items.title: The Web Is More Than Enough
items.author: edward
items.summary: According to Paul Ford's article "The Web Is More Than Enough" on Ftrain, web browsers enable rich app development, and the web is the greatest distribution platform imaginable with features like multilingual support, accessibility infrastructure, and security through the Web Crypto API. Additionally, the web supports high-quality 3D and 2D graphics via WebGL, sound mixing through the Web Audio API, and native-speed code execution with Web Assembly. The sources also mention that Paul Ford launched tinylittleoffice.com, which drew a couple hundred thousand users without incurring any Cloudflare hosting costs.

items.title: DeepX claims inference up to 100B parameters at less than 5 W
items.author: giuliomagnifico
items.summary: DeepX claims its second-generation AI accelerator, the DX-M2, can perform inference of models with up to 100 billion parameters at less than 5 W. This is achieved with custom processor-in-memory technology from Samsung, designed to enable generative AI in edge devices like robots and drones. The chip is intended to run models with 20 billion to 100 billion parameters at 10 to 30 tokens per second, within the same power budget as its predecessor, the DX-M1, which is now in mass production for vision applications.

items.title: Drones built to look like birds evaded detection at Air Force tech exercise
items.author: bushwart
items.summary: A wing-flapping drone resembling a crow, developed by Ornadyne, successfully evaded detection during an Air Force tech exercise in the Mojave Desert on September 17, 2026. The O1 ornithopter drone, designed to mimic the flight mechanics of a bird, did not register as an aircraft on counter-drone sensors, instead blending in with the environment by changing its color, wingspan, proportions, and silhouette to match native bird species. The test was part of the military's annual "Game of Drones" event at Edwards Air Force Base, sponsored by the Air Force 412th Test Wing's Experimental Test Force and the Defense Contract Management Agency's Blue List team.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 launch offers
items.author: danc2050
items.summary: The launch offers for Claude Fable 5.2 are $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. The model is designed for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, with a context window of 1 million tokens and a max output of 128K tokens. The sources also mention a 50% discount on input and output for Batch API. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on whether these offers are still active as of today's date.

items.title: The Qlobe: Rotating Quine (2010)
items.author: niceguitars
items.summary: The sources mention "The Qlobe: Rotating Quine (2010)" in the context of a discussion on Hacker News and a YouTube video describing it as an autonomous spinning globe that uses the Earth's magnetic field to keep spinning without any external power source. The YouTube video also notes that the globe's rotational speed is set by its motor, which does not change even with external influences like light or magnetic fields. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the specific details or origin of the Qlobe.

items.title: Show HN: Recalc – Spreadsheet where cells can be Claude Code or Codex terminals
items.author: sshah03

The goal was quite simple, make it easy to use a lead claude code / codex session in a panel on the side, while allowing every cell to also be a terminal session running claude/codex, and make it possible to continue a session in an actual terminal window if I needed to. They can all talk to each other using cells on the grid, named cells, or the MCP server tha
items.summary: Recalc is a spreadsheet where each cell can hold a value, a formula, a terminal command, or a Claude Code or Codex agent. It was created by sshah03 to facilitate the use of AI agents in evaluations and benchmarks. The spreadsheet allows for easy integration of a Claude Code or Codex session in a panel on the side, while also enabling each cell to function as a terminal session running claude/codex. The tool is available for free on GitHub.
